entries.finding: Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): P 14.09292 d; Howard et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..278...52H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HOWARD_ET_AL__2025): a/R* derived by Kepler's third law from its period 14.09292 d, stellar mass 0.84 and radius 0.809 solar units; Mayo et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..136M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAYO_ET_AL__2018): inclination 89.16344 degrees; No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular; Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): transit mid-time 2456907.2322 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 211 min); Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north)..
